cards.text: Korah, a Levite, led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron, and the LORD judged the rebels. The very next day, the people grumbled against Moses and Aaron ANYWAY (Numbers 16). Now the LORD speaks to Moses.
God's plan is simple. Moses is to collect staffs from the Israelites, one from the leader of each tribe.

cards.question: One staff per tribe leader means Moses collects ___ staffs.
Each tribe leader's name gets written on his own staff.
The tribe of Levi gets a staff too. God says the staff of Levi gets ___'s name on it.

cards.text: All the staffs go into the Tent of Meeting, in front of the Testimony, where God meets with Moses. Sticks in a tent. Either a miracle's coming or somebody's going CAMPING.

cards.question: God says the staff of the man He chooses will do something. What will it do?

answers.text: It will turn into a snake

cards.question: God says this will rid Him of the Israelites' constant grumbling against Moses.

cards.text: Moses gathers all twelve staffs, Aaron's among them, and lays them before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony. The next day, he walks back in.

cards.question: One of the twelve staffs in the tent has changed. Whose staff is it?
Aaron's staff isn't just a stick anymore. What does Moses find on it?

cards.text: Friend. I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS and all I grew was dust. This stick spends ONE day in a tent and makes ALMONDS.
Moses carries all twelve staffs out, and all the Israelites see them. Each leader takes his own staff back.

cards.question: Then the LORD gives orders about Aaron's staff. Moses is to hand it back to Aaron to carry.
Instead, Aaron's staff goes back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign. Who is the sign for?
When God explains the sign, He says the people's grumbling is against Him.

cards.text: Moses does exactly what the LORD commands. No arguing, no snooze button. Then the Israelites have something to say to Moses.

cards.question: What do the Israelites cry out to Moses after seeing Aaron's staff?

answers.text: That they are all lost and perishing
That they will gladly follow Aaron
That they want to go back to Egypt

cards.question: The Israelites fear that anyone who comes near the ___ of the LORD will die.

cards.text: That's a BIG question hanging in the air, friend, and we're leaving it right there for now. Trust me, this story's not done.

findings.problem: Moses and Aaron first show up here without being introduced. Only Korah gets a description (a Levite). A baker who starts with this passage isn't told who Moses or Aaron is.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: In Numbers 17:5 God tells Moses the grumbling is "against you." The card narrows that to "against Moses." The context (Numbers 16:41, 'grumbled against Moses and Aaron') suggests the 'you' may include Aaron. The card should keep the text's wording open, for example 'against you' or 'against Moses and Aaron' with the reference.

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 7 already said the chosen staff 'will sprout,' and Numbers 17:8 says the staff 'sprouted.' A baker could argue that 'A few small green leaves' describes sprouting. The right answer also stands out as the only complete, fuller-sounding option.

rule.text: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card only carries a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, and it re-cites Numbers 17:8, which cards 10 and 11 already covered. The joke should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward, such as card 9 or card 13.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: No card tells or asks about 'lest they die' (Numbers 17:10). That phrase is the reason given for the sign, and it sets up the people's cry in 17:12-13 that they are perishing. Without it, card 18 also has no setup and becomes a guess.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 17 gives no context for how the Israelites react, so a thoughtful baker has no basis to choose 'lost and perishing' over 'gladly follow Aaron.' The pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: **The check:** could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card says 'The Israelites fear that...' as a fact. Numbers 17:13 says they declared it and doesn't name a feeling. A guess at their feeling has to be marked as Papa Dorin's own.

rule.text: **Feelings:** He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the word 'tabernacle,' which no earlier card used. Earlier cards say 'Tent of Meeting' and 'Tent of the Testimony.' The baker is guessing wording they haven't seen, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card refers to 'a BIG question hanging in the air,' but no card has told the baker the question in Numbers 17:13 ('Are we all going to perish?'). The card points back to something the baker never saw.

rule.text: **Always give context in the question.** The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line nearly copies the doc's example ('Trust me, friend, this story's not done').

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
